[1] Salla settings, Shipping & delivery: "Auto-assign warehouse by customer city"; "When an order is marked as Completed, the system automatically assigns an available warehouse based on the shipping city." A rule that assigns an order to the location that fulfils it: order routing, core (Salla's own settings). Condition: the section's permission shipping_options_management; no plan gate on the field. [2] Settings, Inventory (multi-warehouses), form shipment_strategy: "Choose how products in a single order are shipped when they come from different branches" (single or multiple shipments), shipping-fee calculation, and "Auto-assign orders to carriers" (lowest cost or priority). That is how an order spanning branches is split and which carrier takes it, next to routing but not itself the assignment of an order to locations. Core, under the inventory section's s:plan-gate, plans team, special, pro.
why: Both lines are Salla's own settings for which location fulfils an order, so core, the strongest placement, holds. [1] auto-assigns a warehouse by the shipping city when the order is marked Completed. [2] is the list in the shipment_strategy form (inventory.json). I first read it only as order splitting and carriers, but it also holds the checkbox ship_unlimited_products_from_default_branch: orders for products without stock limits reduce quantity from the default branch, a rule on the shipping location, as the claim reads it. The scope team;special;pro on the inventory entry matches the section's s:plan-gate (plans team, special, pro). [1] has no plan gate, only the section permission shipping_options_management, so no scope there is right.

why: Core is right: WooCommerce core's own feature imports and exports settings in bulk. The scope is wrong to be empty. WooCommerce names the feature "Blueprint (beta)", and the definitions count a beta, and a feature flag, as scope. The claim's reading notes the beta badge but drops it by its own convention (a released flag with a beta badge), which the source does not state. Missing scope: beta (Blueprint (beta)), a feature flag (blueprint) that is on by default (enabled_by_default true, is_experimental false, disable_ui false) and that the merchant can switch off. Because it is on by default, the beta limits maturity, not which stores have it.
